newsitem.title: GERMANY: Airlines wrong to opt for surcharge - German GSA.
newsitem.headline: Airlines wrong to opt for surcharge - German GSA.

text.p: Airlines were wrong to opt for cargo fuel surcharges instead of higher rates to cover increasing fuel costs, a leading German cargo sales agent said.

Lothar Schaller, sales manager Germany of the country's largest gsa, Aerotrans Luftfahrtagentur GmbH, said it would have made more sense to raise rates instead of a surcharge which is just a temporary hike.
"If the operational costs of an airline increase then the price should be changed," he told Reuters in an interview.
"A fuel surcharge is non-commissionable, is not easy for forwarders to explain to clients and what about road feeder services?" he asked.
"I would be for increased rates and that would be better in the long-term," he added.
The general cargo fuel surcharge of 10 U.S. cents per kilo has already been criticised by shippers in Germany, the Netherlands, France and the UK.
Some forwarders have also said they are unhappy at the short notice given to pass on the rise to their clients. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
